Scoring speech items in a patient who is simply drowsy.
name: Field Assessment Stroke Triage for Emergency Destination

version.label: FAST-ED (Lima et al. 2016)
version.detail: Five NIHSS-derived items, 0–9. Denial/neglect uses the published definitions; some EMS services use local question-based adaptations, which are not combined here.

purpose: Prehospital estimation of large vessel occlusion likelihood in suspected stroke.
intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected acute stroke, assessed by trained prehospital clinicians.

calculatorNotice.title: Screening scale
calculatorNotice.message: Destination thresholds are set by regional stroke protocols. FAST-ED does not confirm a vessel occlusion.

options.label: Drift or some effort against gravity
No effort against gravity or no movement
Extinction to bilateral simultaneous stimulation in only one sensory modality
Does not recognise own hand or orients only to one side of the body

resultStates.label: No deficit on FAST-ED items
resultStates.summary: No deficit on the FAST-ED items at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: A score of 0 does not exclude stroke.

resultStates.label: FAST-ED {total}
resultStates.summary: Higher scores indicate more cortical and motor signs associated with large vessel occlusion.
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full assessment and the regional stroke pathway.

clinicalContext.text: Derived from NIHSS items with high predictive value for large vessel occlusion.

clinicalInsights.text: Denial or neglect suggests a cortical (often right-hemisphere) syndrome.
Re-assess on arrival; deficits can evolve during transport.

limitations.text: Does not distinguish ischaemia from haemorrhage or stroke mimics.

limitations: Posterior circulation occlusions may score low.
Local EMS adaptations of the neglect item differ from the published definitions.

confounders.effect: Seizure, hypoglycaemia or migraine can produce scorable deficits.

guideSections.what: A five-item prehospital scale (facial palsy, arm weakness, speech, eye deviation, denial/neglect), 0–9.
guideSections.whenToUse: Prehospital assessment of suspected stroke within a regional protocol.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score each item from the examination. Add the five item scores.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A screening scale; confirmation requires vascular imaging.

sources.citation: Lima FO, Silva GS, Furie KL, et al. Field Assessment Stroke Triage for Emergency Destination: a simple and accurate prehospital scale to detect large vessel occlusion strokes. Stroke. 2016;47(8):1997-2002.
